album.title: Radif of Persian Music on Setar II

just_intervals.note: measured octave minus 1200 ¢, register to register

progression.narrative: The performance opens on Eb4 and dwells most on Eb in Mokhalef. Masnavi-ye Mokhalef (2:10.7) introduces Gk, centred on Eb. The line peaks at Gk4 (387.0 Hz) at 2:30.7. It closes on Eb4, not the tonic (Eb4 → Eb4 → Dk4 → Eb4 → Eb4 → Eb4).

theory_fit.name: 12-tone equal temperament
theory_fit.description: Reference only: distance from the semitone grid.

theory_fit.name: Vaziri 24-tone equal temperament
theory_fit.description: Quarter-tone grid (koron/sori = exactly 50 ¢ from the natural note).

theory_fit.name: Pythagorean / Safi al-Din
theory_fit.description: Nearest note of the 17-note gamut generated by pure fifths (±8) from the tonic.

theory_fit.name: Farhat interval classes
theory_fit.description: Interval classes Hormoz Farhat measured in performance practice ("The Dastgah Concept in Persian Music", 1990). Approximate centres.

flags: tonic Gk set in the catalog (Segah's finalis G koron (193.5 Hz): six of the suite's nine tracks voted it and the pitch set fits from it (0, 142, 355, 497, 700, 852, 1065 cents). The vote picked the 4th above; Mokhalef moves in a mode of its own centred on the 6th (Farhat 1990, p. 54), which takes 66 % of this track's sounding time. Inference, not yet by ear); the runs' vote favoured 258.2 Hz (Cs)
